title: Two Math Fighters — DRAGO × ROCKY
question: What became useful when two mathematical research tracks developed differently—and what do their saved tests actually show?
finding: The owner reports complementary broad/investigative and direct/simplifying styles. Nine source-backed dossiers preserve particular useful findings, failures and costs without treating them as a controlled speed ranking.
method: Retrospective editorial selection of saved reports, inputs, results and proof documents; no historical scientific code, solver, experiment, benchmark or proof audit rerun. Only source-file identity, document layout and package integrity checked.
claim_scope: Attributed working observations plus the selected historical finite results and conditional arguments. Unequal starting resources, distinct tasks, later agenda changes and authorized shared episodes prevent causal model or speed comparisons.
limitations: Retrospective and selectively recovered corpus, not a complete final archive census or preregistered neutral sample.
Rocky daily notebook examples end November 3; later checkpoint bodies are outside this recovered edition. Selected Drago repair is dated November 4.
Some dossiers include full selected inputs/code/results; others are report-supported and do not include their large raw archives.
Historical independent checks are not recast as external peer review or fresh mathematical certification.
No model-weight training, universal speed ranking, tested combined-team advantage, or P versus NP resolution established.
Publication and official builder/schema validation remain separate pending steps.
